entries.answer: An IP address identifies a device on a network, and IPv4 uses four numbers from 0 to 255 while IPv6 uses a far larger space. The important part is the split into network and host portions, because that split is what a router uses to decide whether to forward a packet or answer it itself. Private ranges are reserved for internal networks and are not routable publicly, which is why a home router always has one.

patterns: why is tcp slower than udp
what is the three way handshake
entries.answer: TCP is a transport protocol that delivers every byte in order and retransmits anything lost, which is what makes it reliable. It establishes a connection with a handshake before any data flows, and that setup cost is why it is slower than UDP where a late packet is worse than a lost one. HTTP, SSH and most database traffic run over it.

patterns: when to use udp instead of tcp
entries.answer: UDP sends data without connecting, ordering or retransmitting, which makes it fast and cheap but not reliable. That trade is correct for live things where a late packet is worthless, such as a video call, a game or a DNS lookup. A packet lost in a video call is invisible, while the same packet lost in a file transfer means a corrupt file.

entries.answer: DNS translates a human name like a domain into an IP address a machine can route to, which is why it is called the phonebook of the internet. The lookup is hierarchical, so a resolver asks a root, which points at a top-level domain server, which points at the authoritative one. Other record types matter too, as MX points at mail servers and CNAME aliases one name to another.

entries.answer: A router forwards packets between different networks, and a home router also assigns addresses, runs the wireless access point, bridges to the wired ports, and usually runs NAT. NAT is the part people forget, and it is why a home network can share one public address among many devices by rewriting them all to look like the same machine.

patterns: can a firewall stop all attacks
entries.answer: A firewall enforces a rule set about which connections are allowed in or out, filtering by address, port and sometimes by inspecting the traffic. Stateful firewalls remember which connections were opened from inside and let the returning traffic through, which is why an unsolicited incoming connection is usually dropped. It is a perimeter control rather than a guarantee, because traffic that is allowed can still carry something harmful.

entries.answer: Latency is the delay before data begins to arrive, and it is not the same as bandwidth, which is how much can arrive at once. A fast connection with high latency feels worse for interactive work than a slow one with low latency, because every round trip is felt. Physical distance sets a floor, since light cannot beat its own speed in glass.

patterns: does a vpn make you anonymous
entries.answer: A VPN builds an encrypted tunnel between two points so that traffic appears to come from somewhere else, which hides it from the local network but not from the endpoints. A full VPN shifts trust from your internet provider to the VPN operator, which is a real trade rather than a pure gain. It does not make you anonymous, because the service you connect to can still see you.
